explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/931: Erdős thought that perhaps equal prime factors force n₂ > 2(n₁+k₁); the page says this is false as stated (AlphaProof counterexample) but may have been intended up to finitely many counterexamples. The Lean statement: for k₁ ≥ k₂ ≥ 3 the set of pairs with n₁+k₁ ≤ n₂ ≤ 2(n₁+k₁) and equal prime factor sets is finite, i.e. the bound n₂ > 2(n₁+k₁) holds with finitely many exceptions for each (k₁,k₂). This is the weakened question described on the page, and the docstring says so. Faithful.
